newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ says still concerned at petrol price margins.
newsitem.headline: NZ says still concerned at petrol price margins.

text.p: New Zealand Energy Minister Max Bradford on Wednesday reiterated concerns that petrol retail prices were trending higher in an atmosphere of limited competition in the country.
Bradford said in a statement commenting on a national energy review that both he and consumers would be pleased to see a new supplier in the market.
"I would encourage companies to look at the New Zealand petrol market. The signs are there is money to be made."

Bradford said the latest analysis of petrol importers' margins showed per-litre retail prices, excluding taxes, had been rising by nearly one NZ cent per year relative to international prices for several years.

"Consultants are currently completing a study to identify barriers to entry to the New Zealand petrol market. The report, when released, will be a useful fund of information to potential market entrants," he added.
About 60 percent of New Zealand's petrol stations are owned by the so-called "big four" majors, British Petroleum Co Plc, Mobil Corp, Shell and Caltex, with most of the rest under contract to them.

Earlier this year a series of newspaper articles speculated that local oil company Fletcher Energy, potentially in cooperation with supermarket retailer Progressive Enterprises, was readying an assault on the market.
However, both firms denied they had any immediate plans.
